plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.

conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and focuses on broad market exposure and income, aiming for lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Reduce exposure to high-beta software (METU, PLTU) and semiconductors (MUU).
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to manage concentration.
Add an inverse tech ETF (TECS) for potential downside protection.

balanced.read: This balanced strategy targets approximately 2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a hedging instrument. It aims for risk-first growth, accepting moderate drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU).
Trim income ETF (QQQI) to fund leverage.
Add an inverse tech ETF (TECS) for potential hedging.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.

aggressive.read: This aggressive strategy targets around 4% monthly return by increasing leverage and concentration in high-conviction names and leveraged ETFs. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the risks associated with leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, PLTU, MUU).
Increase allocation to income ETF (QQQI) for distributions.
Add to broad index ETF (SPY) for stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and low drawdowns.

income.read: This income-focused strategy targets around 1% monthly return by prioritizing income-generating ETFs and broad market exposure. It aims for low drawdowns and reliable monthly distributions, with capital preservation as a key objective.
